messages:
Alex P.: Quick sync — handing off the per-model latency & throughput dashboard work. We need a clear runtime->ingest label contract and sampling guidance. Proposed metrics: P50/P95/P99 (from hist), TTFT (seconds), tokens/sec. cc @Maria G. @Kevin L.

Maria G.: Console will own the panels/UX. Runtime should own metric emission. We need label set nailed down: model_id, model_display, route, env, pool_id, route_version. Keep it minimal. :ok_hand:

Kevin L.: +1. Prefer runtime emit raw histograms (latency buckets) + counters for tokens. Summaries are painful to aggregate. Can we standardize bucket boundaries?

Sandeep R.: Ingest constraints: histograms at high-cardinality are expensive. If we take histograms, we should aggregate client-side to a 10s window and only emit aggregated counts per (model,route,env,pool). Otherwise fall back to quantiles emitted at controlled rate.

Alex P.: Agreed. How about a default bucket set we maintain in code? Runtime will emit buckets with those boundaries. For hosted vs dedicated: hosted default sampling 1/10, dedicated full emission. Sampling should be config per customer.

Kevin L.: Bucket proposal (draft):
```
latency_buckets_ms = [1,2,5,10,20,50,100,200,500,1000,2000,5000]
```
Emit as seconds in metric names though. Also tokens counter: redwood_request_tokens_total{model_id,route,env}.

Maria G.: Console needs stable model_display (human friendly) and model_id (internal). We'll resolve mapping in ingest. Also need route_version label for rollout dashboards (canary vs stable).

Sandeep R.: We can add route_version but warn about cardinality explosion. Suggest allow route_version only when canary flag true; otherwise empty or "stable".

Alex P.: For TTFT, runtime can emit a gauge duration per request: redwood_request_ttft_seconds. Is that OK for ingest?

Sandeep R.: Gauges per request are fine if rate-limited. Better to emit aggregated TTFT histogram per 10s window to avoid per-request spikes.

Kevin L.: For tokens/sec we can calculate from counter diffs ingested, but we need a consistent scrape/aggregation window. We'll document that console computes tokens/sec as delta(tokens_total)/window_seconds. Recommend window = 60s.

Maria G.: Dashboard layout (high level):
- Top row: global KPIs (p50/p95/p99 latency across selected model or route, TTFT avg)
- Middle: per-route heatmap tokens/sec and tail latency (p99)
- Bottom: rollout view showing route_version split, canary vs baseline comparison + error rates
We also want a per-model compact card for product pages.

Alex P.: Alerts: SRE suggests alert on p99 > threshold AND tokens/sec sustained drop. Also alert on divergence between route baselines during rollout.

Kevin L.: We'll add a small derived metric: route_latency_regression_score which compares canary p95 vs baseline p95. That can drive rollout aborts/flags.

Sandeep R.: From ingest side, schema PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/472 — it includes histogram buckets and label set. ingest-bot: please review.

ingest-bot: schema PR #472 created by Sandeep R. — https://github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/472 :sparkles:

console-bot: dashboard mock uploaded: https://grafana.company.internal/d/abcd1234/per-model-latency-ux — feedback needed by Tue EOD.

Maria G.: Nice. Action items: (1) Alex — runtime PR to add standard buckets + route_version config (due Fri). (2) Sandeep — finalize ingest aggregation and sampling config (PR #472). (3) Kevin — docs for console aggregation windows and regression_score formula. (4) Maria — dashboard mock updates and alert thresholds.

Alex P.: I'll own the runtime PR. Quick Q: should we tag metrics with pool_id or gpu_type to help correlate perf with hardware?

Sandeep R.: pool_id is fine. GPU type increases cardinality — prefer mapping in metadata service instead of metric label if you can.

Kevin L.: final thought: add an example metric contract snippet for devs to copy into SDKs. E.g.
```
# metrics emitted per request (sampled or aggregated)
redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket{model_id="gpt-4x",route="chat",env="prod",le="0.1"} 42
redwood_request_tokens_total{model_id="gpt-4x",route="chat",env="prod"} 1234
redwood_request_ttft_seconds_sum{model_id="gpt-4x",route="chat",env="prod"} 3.21
redwood_request_ttft_seconds_count{model_id="gpt-4x",route="chat",env="prod"} 2
```
Keep it easy to copy.

Maria G.: Sounds good. Let's sync Mon 10am for final cross-team signoff. :memo: :calendar:

Alex P.: Thanks everyone — will open the runtime PR today and ping when ready. :rocket:
